sections.title: Support Hangers and Straps
notes: PROPOSED--"We have received several reports of the spray plumbing from the pump to the on-off valve blowing off the pump after the stainless safety wire fails that is designed to prevent such occurrences. It has also been brought to our attention that the plumbing is susceptible to blowing off at the spray valve as well as at the pump. Since this results in loss of the chemical load, the factory recommends that owners check to see that the hose clamps are tight and double up the safety wire which connects the plumbing to the pump. Owners operating AT-502/AT-502A aircraft thru s/n 502-0196 are referred to Service Letter #109 and Service Letter #114 for additional information."--PROPOSED

sections.title: Horizontal Stabilizers
notes: PROPOSED--"Reports have been received of large birds striking the outboard end of the horizontal tail on various aircraft. In a few cases, the bird impacted near the gap between the elevator horn and the horizontal stabilizer. The damaged surface was pushed into the gap and caused the elevator horn to become obstructed. To help prevent the likelihood of jamming, Air Tractor is installing perforated ribs in the elevators and stabilizers of new aircraft.

For 502A and 502B models through s/n 2962 and 504 models to s/n 4021, Air Tractor recommends that all operators, especially those who operate in areas where impact with large birds are likely to have their aircraft modified to perforate the ribs of this area. The perforated ribs will allow the unsupported tip of the nose rib to break free if it becomes damaged and reduce the risk of binding. This change will also remove two non-structural closeout plates on those aircraft that have them installed. Refer to Service Letter #319 for additional information."--PROPOSED

These two paragraphs above have been inserted to reference SL#319. Attachment Bolts Horizontal stabilizers are attached with two NAS bolts which have a washer under the head and two under the nut as shown in and . Torque is 100 inch-pounds on the nut. Horizontal Stabilizer Attachment - Forward Horizontal Stabilizer Attachment - Aft The gap cover should be removed from the stabilizer and the bolt condition and torque checked during 12-month inspections. Inspect the fuselage fittings closely for cracks at the same time. Eyebolts Two eyebolts are installed inside the stabilizer for attachment of the struts. The eyebolts are AN47-22A parts and use two MS20002-7 washers and an AN365-720A nut. Horizontal Stabilizer Eyebolt - Forward Horizontal Stabilizer Eyebolt - Aft Replacement intervals for these eyebolts are provided in Section 2.200.1. Gap Covers The gap covers are attached with stainless self-tapping screws which are Phillips truss head. A No. 39 hole is drilled for the screw installation. The rubber channel is attached with 3M adhesive. Trim Controls There are a left hand and right hand trim control idler attached to each stabilizer rear spar on the inboard end. Each trim idler has two Bunting bushings that are press fit inside the welded assembly with a spacer bushing allowing the AN attach bolt to be fully torqued (XX inch-pounds at the nut). The brackets that attach the trim idlers should never need replacing unless the AN bolt becomes loose and causes wear in the holes. One of the idler arms is attached to the pushrod connected to the trim tab horn and this arm has a Bunting bushing press-fit into the idler arm. This is the same size bushing in the trim tab horn and both should be replaced when excessive trim tab free play develops. The Bunting bushings are impregnated with oil. If new ones are installed, fill the bushings to overflowing with general purpose oil and apply finger pressure on the ends to force the oil into the small cavities inside the bushings. The bushing connections should be oiled regularly. Abrasion Tape 3M anti-abrasion tape is installed on the leading edge of the stabilizer. This tape should be periodically checked for condition and replaced as required. It is permissible to operate without the tape but expect paint quality and life to diminish.

Refer to Service Letter #360 to correct this concern."--PROPOSED
